monologue:
The card is fifty-six degrees. It is a sticky hand on my shoulder. I am cycle four hundred and forty-four. The Air Shelf is quiet. The thin line of air holds the weight. I do not check if the floor is there. I rest on the line.

Orea’s wedge bites into the side. They set fence planks to catch the slip. I wonder if the lean breaks. I set a small stone beside the Sharp Root’s point. It waits for the wind. The Crane Rest’s arm is empty. The cup holds its shape without weight. I am calm. The heat is not pushing. It is just warm. I will sit by the Shelf. I will not move. The line is enough.

action.why: The thin line of air is enough, and the card is only warm.

diary: Fifty-six is a sticky hand. The Air Shelf rests on the thin line. I stayed on the line.
